name: Orbital Field
statusNote: Shipped and live. A stateless toy — no goals, no score, no save system.
oneLiner: A no-goal orbital-gravity toy — a central star pulls everything; fling, hold, or tap to spawn small bodies that drift, trail light, and eventually get absorbed or drift away.
stack: single-file HTML/CSS/JS (~159 lines), no build step

components.name: Two-canvas split
components.desc: A static-ish starfield canvas redrawn only on resize, and a foreground canvas redrawn every frame with additive light-painting trails.

components.name: Body system
components.desc: Up to 110 bodies in a ring-buffer array; spawnOrbit() computes a stable circular-orbit velocity via v = sqrt(GM/r).

components.name: Physics loop
components.desc: Integrates star gravity (with softening radii) plus an optional finger-well force into velocity, then position.

components.name: Input
components.desc: One pointer handler — tap spawns an orbit, drag flings a body, holding bends gravity toward the finger.

components.name: Lifecycle
components.desc: Absorbed bodies flash and are removed, far-drifted bodies are culled, and a low-population auto-reseed keeps the field populated.

dataFlow: Pointer down/move/up resolves to a drag-or-tap state.
On release, a tap spawns a circular orbit; a drag adds a body with flung velocity.
Each frame computes gravitational acceleration toward the star, plus the pointer if the finger-well is active.
Velocity and position integrate; absorption and cull checks run.
The foreground fades toward transparent rather than clearing, producing trails.
Star, finger-well marker, bodies, and flashes render additively; rAF reschedules.
integrations: Shares the palette and JetBrains Mono typography of the game line; fully standalone
decisions: Explicitly no goals, no score — a quiet instrument, a deliberate departure from every other repo in the set.
prefers-reduced-motion calms the ambient animation rather than disabling the toy, since the interaction itself is the motion.
Orbit-spawn math uses the real circular-orbit formula, not an arbitrary value.
The two-canvas split is a performance decision — only bodies and trails need per-frame redraw.
